name: Contact lens hygiene break

angle.text: Users pause lens wear and clean lenses carefully to get clearer, whiter-looking eyes. It appears in looksmaxxing lists under eye whites. Lens-related redness is a recognised clinical topic, but no study tests this routine for appearance.

summary: Pausing lens wear and cleaning properly is aimed at fewer red eyes; no study tests it for looks.
note: Persistent redness or pain warrants an eye doctor, per general guidance.
currentQuick:
This is the practice of taking time off from contact lenses and keeping them clean so the eyes look less red.
Sources describe hygiene standards and note a day without lenses can ease discomfort, but no study tests breaks for appearance.
How it works: Lens wear can cause irritation and inflammation; resting the eye and good cleaning aim to reduce it.
Risks and caveats: Poor hygiene and overnight wear are linked to infections and corneal problems; severe or lasting symptoms call for an eye doctor.
deepLead:
A contact lens hygiene break refers to pausing contact lens wear and following careful lens hygiene to reduce eye redness. It appears in looksmaxxing lists as a way to get fewer red eyes.
Wikipedia's contact lens article reports that the American Academy of Ophthalmology recommends the rub-and-rinse cleaning method and replacing lens cases at least every three months, and that wearing lenses past their replacement schedule or sleeping in daily-wear lenses raises infection risk. It also says that if discomfort persists, taking a day off from wear may resolve it, and that severe or lasting discomfort should be checked by an eye doctor.

name: Chest resonance training

angle.text: Users practise speaking from the chest to sound deeper and fuller, borrowing the chest voice idea from singing instruction. Acoustics sources describe the chest as adding little resonance, and the appearance use itself has not been trialled.

summary: Speaking 'from the chest' for a deeper voice; acoustics sources say the chest adds little resonance, and no appearance trials exist.
note: Acoustics references report the chest is not a significant resonator; felt vibration is mostly sensory feedback.
currentQuick:
Chest resonance training is the practice of speaking so that vibration is felt in the upper chest, in hopes of sounding deeper and fuller. It draws on the singing-teacher idea of a 'chest voice'.
Reference works on voice acoustics say the chest contributes little to the actual resonance of the voice, though the felt vibration can be useful feedback. No trials have tested the practice for appearance purposes.
How it works: Practitioners combine relaxed breathing, a lower habitual pitch and attention to chest vibration. Acoustically, pitch is set by vocal fold length and tension, and timbre by the pharynx and mouth.
Risks and caveats: Little risk is documented for gentle practice. Singing sources note that forcing chest voice into high notes may strain the voice.
deepLead:
Chest resonance training is a looksmaxxing-adjacent voice practice in which a person tries to speak "from the chest" in order to produce a deeper, fuller-sounding voice. The phrase is also used in singing instruction, where teachers have long described a "chest voice" and the sensation of vibration in the upper torso.
Acoustics references describe the matter differently from many voice books. Wikipedia's article on vocal resonation states that the chest is not an effective resonator and makes no significant contribution to the voice's resonance, although strong vibrations can be felt there and "chest" is also used as a perceptual term for a dark, warm vocal colour. Vocal pedagogy sources note that modern teaching increasingly treats chest and head sensations as resonance experiences rather than registers.
No published clinical studies were found that test chest resonance training as a way of lowering voice pitch for appearance purposes.

name: Lowering pitch exercises

angle.text: Users train a lower speaking pitch to sound deeper or more masculine without surgery or drugs. Pitch is measurable and voice training is studied in clinical settings, but trials for this appearance goal are absent.

summary: Practising a lower speaking pitch for a deeper voice; physiology sets limits and no appearance trials exist.
note: Pitch range is set largely by vocal fold size; no trials in healthy speakers.
currentQuick:
Lowering pitch exercises are voice practices such as gliding down, humming and reading at a lower pitch, used to sound deeper.
References describe pitch as depending mainly on vocal fold length and tension. No published trials test these exercises for appearance in healthy speakers.
How it works: Laryngeal muscles adjust fold length and tension; exercises aim to make a lower habitual pitch comfortable.
Risks and caveats: No documented harms from gentle practice were found; pedagogy sources caution against forcing the voice beyond a comfortable range.
deepLead:
Lowering pitch exercises are vocal practices that people use to speak at a lower fundamental frequency, usually to sound deeper or more masculine. They appear in looksmaxxing discussion of voice as a way to change a perceived trait without surgery or drugs.
Pitch depends on how quickly the vocal folds vibrate, which in turn depends on fold length, mass and tension. Longer, larger folds vibrate more slowly, and adult male folds are longer than adult female folds. Typical adult male speech fundamentals are reported between about 90 and 155 Hz and female between about 165 and 255 Hz.
No published clinical studies were found that test lowering-pitch exercises in healthy speakers for appearance purposes.

name: Vocal fry and glottal control

angle.text: Some users control vocal fry to make their voice sound lower. Perception studies of creaky voice exist, but none test it as a way to improve vocal attractiveness.

summary: Using creaky low-register phonation for a lower sound; perception studies exist but none test it for looks.
note: Excessive use may signal a voice disorder; listener studies report mixed social perceptions.
currentQuick:
Vocal fry is the lowest vocal register, a slow popping sound from loose glottal closure. Some people try to use it to sound lower.
Research covers how it is used and perceived, but no trials test it as an appearance method.
How it works: Slack, compressed vocal folds vibrate irregularly at very low frequency.
Risks and caveats: Occasional use is generally considered normal; excessive use may signal a voice disorder. One study reported negative listener ratings.
deepLead:
Vocal fry, also called creaky voice or glottal fry, is the lowest vocal register, produced with loose glottal closure that yields a slow, popping or rattling sound at very low frequency. In looksmaxxing voice discussion, some people try to control it to make their voice sound lower.
Researchers describe fry as a normal part of the pitch range that is not by itself a laryngeal pathology, though excessive use may signal a voice disorder. Studies of listener perception are mixed in framing: one 2014 study reported that speakers using fry were rated less competent, less trustworthy and less attractive, though the study has been criticised for using imitators.
No clinical studies were found that test fry as a method of appearance enhancement.

name: Diaphragmatic breathing

angle.text: Users practise belly breathing to support the voice and speak with more depth and presence. It is studied for stress and respiratory care, while its effect on how a voice sounds in appearance terms is untested.

summary: Belly breathing for breath support and a deeper voice; studied for stress and lungs, not for voice appearance.
note: Evidence concerns stress and respiratory use; no trials for voice pitch.
currentQuick:
Diaphragmatic breathing uses the diaphragm for slow, deep breaths. It is used for relaxation, respiratory conditions and breath support in singing and speaking.
Research looks at stress and breathing symptoms; none tests it for deepening the voice.
How it works: The diaphragm descends on inhalation, expanding the abdomen, and relaxes on exhalation. Voice teachers describe controlled exhalation as underpinning steady phonation.
Risks and caveats: No serious adverse effects are described in the reference material reviewed.
deepLead:
Diaphragmatic breathing, also called belly or abdominal breathing, is a technique that uses the diaphragm to take deep breaths, typically by inhaling slowly through the nose and exhaling through pursed lips. It is used in respiratory care, in stress and anxiety management, and in voice training, where it is associated with breath support.
In looksmaxxing discussion of the voice, it is mentioned as a way to improve breath control and to deepen vocal tone. Grokipedia states that it is integrated into voice training for men to address insufficient breath support and to deepen tone through chest resonance and breath control. Acoustics references, by contrast, report that the chest contributes little to vocal resonance, and no studies were found testing diaphragmatic breathing for changing voice pitch or appearance.
Published research examines it mainly for relaxation, stress and respiratory conditions.

name: Voice coach / speech therapy

angle.text: People hire voice coaches or speech-language pathologists to change pitch, quality and delivery, a route also used in transgender voice therapy. The clinical field is real and established; trials specific to looksmaxxing goals are absent.

summary: Professional voice therapy or coaching to change how a voice sounds; real clinical field, but no appearance trials.
note: Evidence for voice therapy is mainly in voice disorders, not appearance.
currentQuick:
Voice coaching and speech therapy are professional services, from speech-language pathologists or voice teachers, for changing voice quality or function.
Evidence is mainly in voice disorders and is described as limited; none tests appearance goals in healthy people.
How it works: Therapists and teachers work on breath, pitch, resonance and vocal fold closure through guided exercises.
Risks and caveats: No notable harms are documented in the reviewed references.
deepLead:
Voice coaching and speech therapy refer to professional services used to change how a voice sounds or functions. Voice therapy is provided mainly by speech-language pathologists, who target vocal parameters such as vocal fold closure, pitch, volume and quality, chiefly to manage voice disorders, but also to change overall voice quality, as in transgender voice therapy. Vocal pedagogy, taught by voice teachers, is the related field focused on singing.
In looksmaxxing discussion, professional voice help is mentioned as a route to a different-sounding voice. Published evidence on voice therapy is described as limited and varies by method. No studies were found testing voice coaching for appearance in people without voice disorders.

name: Singing lessons

angle.text: Users take singing lessons to gain voice control, range and a deeper or more resonant speaking voice. Singing instruction is studied for wellbeing and lung function, not for changing how a speaking voice comes across.

summary: Lessons in vocal technique for control and range; studied for wellbeing and lungs, not for changing how your voice looks or sounds in speech.
note: No studies on lessons for deepening the speaking voice.
currentQuick:
Singing lessons teach breath support, resonance, articulation and range through guided exercises with a voice teacher.
Studies have looked at wellbeing, respiratory health and voice measures in singers; none tests lessons for appearance goals.
How it works: Teachers help students link internal sensations to the sound produced and extend range gradually from a comfortable middle range.
Risks and caveats: Singing sources note that overusing chest voice on high notes can cause forcing and may lead to vocal deterioration.
deepLead:
Singing lessons are instruction in vocal technique from a voice teacher, covering breath support, phonation, resonance, articulation and range. In looksmaxxing culture they are mentioned as a way to gain voice control and range, including a deeper or more resonant speaking voice.
Wikipedia describes singing training as systematic practice of exercises for warm-ups, range extension, dynamics and agility, with teachers helping students match internal sensations to the sound produced. Research on lessons has examined well-being, respiratory health and voice measures; no studies were found testing lessons for changing speaking pitch for appearance.

name: Humming exercises

angle.text: Users hum as a vocal warm-up before speaking or singing to get a smoother, more resonant sound. It is popular in voice-training circles, with little research on appearance-related outcomes.

summary: Closed-mouth humming used as a vocal warm-up; popular in voice-training circles, with little appearance-specific research.
note: Evidence is for general vocal warm-up, not for changing how a voice is perceived.
currentQuick:
Humming exercises involve producing a sustained tone with the lips closed, so sound resonates in the head and throat and passes through the nose. In voice-improvement discussions it is mentioned as a gentle warm-up before speaking or singing.
The sources reviewed describe humming in general terms and do not cover it as a vocal warm-up; no studies on humming specifically as an appearance or voice-attractiveness practice were found.
How it works: A hum is made with the mouth closed, so the tone resonates in the nasal and throat passages. Practitioners describe the closed-mouth position as a low-effort way to begin phonating.
Risks and caveats: No specific risks are documented in the sources reviewed. Voice clinicians generally advise that any vocal practice that causes pain or hoarseness be stopped, which is general guidance rather than a finding about humming.
deepLead:
A hum is a wordless tone produced with the mouth closed, so the sound passes through the nose. In looksmaxxing and voice-improvement discussions, humming exercises are described as a vocal warm-up: a way to start phonation gently before speaking or singing.
The reference material on humming consists of general descriptions of the sound and its cultural and evolutionary interpretations; it does not examine humming as a voice-training technique. No studies were found testing humming exercises for changing perceived vocal attractiveness or authority.

name: Straw phonation

angle.text: Users voice through a narrow straw as a warm-up and training drill for a clearer, more controlled voice. It belongs to SOVT exercises with real clinical research; vocal attractiveness has not been tested.

summary: Voicing through a narrow straw, a voice-therapy exercise with real clinical research, though not tested for vocal attractiveness.
note: Studies concern voice quality and vocal fatigue in singers and patients, not perceived attractiveness.
currentQuick:
Straw phonation means making voiced sound while blowing through a narrow straw, which partly closes the vocal tract. It belongs to a family of semi-occluded vocal tract (SOVT) exercises used by voice teachers and speech-language pathologists, and some online voice-improvement communities have adopted it as a warm-up.
Published studies have examined its immediate effects and short therapy programmes in singers and people with voice disorders. Results are mostly short-term and in small samples, and none targets appearance or perceived attractiveness.
How it works: Narrowing the opening at the lips or straw changes air pressure and airflow in the vocal tract and at the vocal folds. Imaging and aerodynamic studies in singers have measured changes in vocal tract shape and glottal function during and after the exercise.[1][4]
Risks and caveats: The reviewed studies do not report notable harms. Researchers describe the exercises as used for habilitation and rehabilitation of the voice.[3] Anyone with a voice disorder is generally directed by clinicians to a speech-language pathologist.
deepLead:
Straw phonation is an exercise in which a person produces voiced sound through a narrow straw or tube. It is one of several semi-occluded vocal tract (SOVT) exercises, which partly obstruct the mouth opening during phonation, and its use in voice training and therapy has grown over roughly two decades.
Research has measured its immediate effects on vocal tract and glottal function, aerodynamic and electroglottographic parameters, and its use in therapy programmes for dysphonia and vocal fatigue. These studies address voice quality and function rather than perceived attractiveness or authority, which communities interested in voice looksmaxxing sometimes discuss.

name: Resonance tuning (formant)

angle.text: Voice-improvement communities adjust vocal tract shape to move formants and change timbre, aiming for a deeper or more masculine sound. Formant acoustics is well established; the practice as a looksmaxxing method is untested.

summary: Shaping vocal tract resonances (formants) to change vocal timbre; grounded in voice acoustics, untested as a looksmaxxing practice.
note: Formant acoustics is established science; claims about perceived attractiveness are untested here.
currentQuick:
Resonance tuning refers to adjusting the shape of the throat and mouth so that vocal tract resonances, called formants, shift and give the voice a different timbre. Voice-modification communities discuss it as a way to alter how a voice sounds.
The underlying acoustics is well described, but no studies were found testing deliberate tuning as an appearance-related practice.
How it works: Formants are broad spectral peaks created by acoustic resonance in the vocal tract; changes in mouth and lip shape move them, for example lip rounding lowers formants.[1] Vowels are mostly identified by the first two formants.[1]
Risks and caveats: No risks are documented in the sources reviewed.
deepLead:
Formants are broad peaks in the sound spectrum arising from acoustic resonance in the vocal tract; they shape the sound produced by the voice but are not sound sources themselves. Resonance tuning is the deliberate adjustment of the vocal tract to move these resonances, and it is discussed in voice-improvement communities as a way to change vocal timbre.
The acoustic background is established: vowel identity depends largely on the first two formants, and trained classical singers show an added peak near 3000 Hz that helps their voices carry over an orchestra. No studies were found evaluating deliberate resonance tuning for perceived attractiveness.

name: Pitch tracking apps

angle.text: Users run pitch tracking apps to see their speaking pitch in Hz while practising a deeper or more resonant voice. They work as a measuring tool; no studies link their use to appearance outcomes.

summary: Apps that read your voice's fundamental frequency in Hz; useful as a meter, with no studies behind appearance claims.
note: Pitch readings can suffer octave errors and noise sensitivity.
currentQuick:
Pitch tracking apps listen to your voice and report its fundamental frequency, usually in hertz or as a note name. They are used to check speaking pitch.
No clinical research evaluates them for appearance or voice-change goals; sources describe only the general technology.
How it works: They apply pitch detection algorithms such as autocorrelation, YIN or spectral methods to estimate the period of the voice signal and convert it to frequency.
Risks and caveats: No direct harms are documented. Documented technical limits include octave errors and noise sensitivity, so readings may be inaccurate.
deepLead:
Pitch tracking apps are smartphone or desktop programs that estimate the fundamental frequency (f0) of a recorded or live voice and display it in hertz or as a musical note. In voice-related appearance and presentation communities they are used to check how high or low a speaking voice sits, for example when practising a deeper or more resonant voice.
Pitch is the listener's subjective impression of how high or low a sound is, while fundamental frequency is the measurable lowest repetition rate of a periodic sound; the two track each other closely but are not identical. Apps typically apply a pitch detection algorithm, a family of methods that estimate the period of a quasi-periodic signal such as speech and invert it to a frequency.
Published sources on these apps as a product category are thin, and no clinical study of a specific looksmaxxing-oriented pitch app was found. The description below therefore covers the underlying technology and its documented limits.

name: Testosterone replacement therapy

angle.text: Medical testosterone is used to restore normal levels in hypogonadism, and users in appearance circles note its virilizing effects including a deeper voice and added muscle. It is studied for muscle and metabolic outcomes in hypogonadal men, not as a voice treatment.

summary: Medical testosterone for low levels; can deepen voice via virilization, studied for muscle and metabolic outcomes in hypogonadal men.
note: Requires diagnosis and monitoring; controlled substance in many countries.
currentQuick:
TRT supplements testosterone in people with diagnosed deficiency. In hypogonadal men, trials report gains in muscle and metabolic markers.
Testosterone can deepen the voice in women or transgender men; voice is not a studied TRT goal.
How it works: Exogenous testosterone restores androgen receptor signaling and suppresses the body's own production through feedback on the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis.
Risks and caveats: Reported risks include raised hematocrit, sleep apnea, fertility suppression, acne, prostate concerns, and cardiovascular questions addressed by TRAVERSE; FDA warnings were revised in 2025.
deepLead:
Testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) is the medical supplementation of testosterone to restore normal levels in people with hypogonadism, mainly men. It can be given by injection, gel, patch, pellet or oral forms.
Testosterone can deepen the voice in some people, such as women or transgender men receiving it, as part of virilization. In men with low testosterone, trials have reported increases in fat-free mass and muscle size.
Safety has been debated: a 2004 review recommended monitoring, and the 2023 TRAVERSE trial studied cardiovascular safety. The FDA changed boxed-warning language in 2025.

name: Testosterone cypionate

angle.text: Testosterone cypionate is a long-acting injectable labelled for hypogonadism, with voice deepening listed among its virilizing effects. Voice change is a side effect of androgen action rather than a studied purpose.

summary: Long-acting injectable testosterone; labelled for hypogonadism, with voice deepening among its listed virilizing effects.
note: Controlled substance; voice changes in women may be permanent.
currentQuick:
Testosterone cypionate is a slow-release injectable form of testosterone used to treat low testosterone and in masculinizing hormone therapy.
Its labelled effects include voice deepening, but no trials test it for appearance or voice goals.
How it works: The ester is slowly released and converted to testosterone, which activates the androgen receptor.
Risks and caveats: Labelled risks include acne, hair loss, fertility suppression, cardiovascular events, clotting, polycythemia concerns and pregnancy contraindication; it is a Schedule III substance in the US.
deepLead:
Testosterone cypionate is a long-acting injectable ester of testosterone, sold mainly as Depo-Testosterone, and a prodrug the body converts to testosterone. It is FDA-labelled for replacement therapy in males with primary or hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
Its listed virilizing effects include acne, body and facial hair growth and deepening of the voice. It is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US, and non-medical use for physique and performance is reported as common.

name: Anavar / oxandrolone voice risk

angle.text: Oxandrolone (Anavar) is an oral anabolic steroid used for muscle and physique; its documented virilizing effects in women include voice deepening, which can be irreversible. Voice change here is an off-target effect, not a studied goal.

Oxandrolone, known as Anavar, is an oral anabolic steroid once used medically for weight recovery and used by some for physique goals, including by women.

Oxandrolone, sold as Oxandrin and colloquially known as Anavar, is an oral synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid. Its article lists voice deepening among the virilizing effects in women, and states that such masculinizing changes can be irreversible.
Women using it for physique purposes have often chosen it because it is described as more anabolic than androgenic, yet its documented risks include voice deepening, hirsutism, menstrual changes, clitoral enlargement and liver effects.

name: Anabolic steroids for voice

angle.text: Androgens including anabolic steroids can lower the voice by acting on the larynx, and some users seek this effect. It is a documented side effect of virilization rather than a studied use, and some changes may be permanent.

summary: Androgens can deepen the voice, but it is a side effect of virilization, not a studied use, and some changes may be irreversible.
note: Voice changes in women may be permanent; controlled substances in the US.
currentQuick:
Anabolic steroids and testosterone can lower the voice because they masculinize the larynx. Some people in appearance communities pursue this effect.
Medical sources list it as a side effect, and no trials test steroids as a voice treatment.
How it works: Androgens act on the androgen receptor, including in laryngeal tissue, thickening and lengthening the vocal folds in the way male puberty does.
Risks and caveats: Documented risks include irreversible virilization in women, acne, hair loss, fertility suppression, lipid and liver effects, and legal restrictions as controlled substances.
deepLead:
Anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) are synthetic androgens that, like testosterone, can lower the voice by acting on the larynx. Voice deepening is listed among the virilizing effects of testosterone and its esters, and in women it is reported as a possible effect of androgens.
Some people in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding circles reportedly view androgens as a way to obtain a deeper voice. Medical sources describe voice deepening as a side effect of treatment, not an indication, and note that androgen-related masculinization in women can be irreversible.
Published material directly on using steroids to change the voice is sparse. A 1964 French-language article titled on synthetic anabolic steroids and the voice exists in the literature.

name: HCG and clomiphene for voice

angle.text: Forum users mention hCG and clomiphene as ways to raise natural testosterone in the hope of a deeper voice. Both are used medically for fertility and off-label for male hypogonadism; no studies address voice.

summary: Two fertility drugs that raise testosterone, floated for voice depth; no voice evidence exists.
note: Prescription drugs with their own documented adverse effects; no voice studies.
currentQuick:
hCG and clomiphene are prescription drugs that raise the body's own testosterone, used for fertility and low testosterone. Some online discussion links them to a deeper voice.
No published studies have tested either drug for voice pitch or resonance in adults.
How it works: hCG mimics luteinizing hormone and stimulates testosterone production in the testes. Clomiphene blocks estrogen feedback in the brain, increasing the signals (GnRH, LH, FSH) that drive testosterone production.
Risks and caveats: Clomiphene can cause visual disturbances, headaches and hot flashes; hCG carries cautions for several conditions. Both are prescription-only in the US, UK and Australia and are banned in competitive sport.
deepLead:
In looksmaxxing discussion, human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) and clomiphene (clomifene) are two prescription drugs sometimes mentioned as ways of raising endogenous testosterone, with the idea that higher testosterone could deepen or maintain a lower voice. Both are used medically for fertility and, off-label, for male hypogonadism.
hCG is a hormone that resembles luteinizing hormone and stimulates the Leydig cells of the testes to make testosterone. Clomiphene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator that blocks estrogen feedback in the hypothalamus, increasing GnRH, FSH and LH release. Encyclopedic sources on both drugs do not describe an effect on adult voice pitch.
No clinical studies of either drug for voice were found. The voice-deepening effect of testosterone is associated with puberty, and the larynx changes of puberty are generally described as lasting.

name: Tongue posture for voice

angle.text: Looksmaxxing communities extend mewing to the voice, proposing that tongue posture changes resonance. The base mewing claim concerns jaw structure and is unproven, and no voice study exists.

summary: Applying mewing to the voice; the base practice is unproven and no voice study exists.
note: Extension of a claim that professional bodies say lacks evidence.
currentQuick:
This is the claim that resting the tongue on the palate, as in mewing, shifts voice resonance. It is a minor offshoot of the mewing trend.
No studies have tested it, and orthodontic bodies say there is no evidence mewing changes the jaw.
How it works: Practitioners hold the tongue against the roof of the mouth, and proponents propose that resulting changes in oral structure alter resonance.
Risks and caveats: The posture itself is not reported as harmful in the sources reviewed, but the broader mewing practice is described as unproven, and its main proponent faced a misconduct finding over child patients.
deepLead:
Tongue posture for voice is the idea, circulated in looksmaxxing communities, that holding the tongue against the roof of the mouth, as in "mewing", changes vocal resonance. It extends the mewing claim, which concerns jaw and facial structure, to the sound of the voice.
Mewing is described by Wikipedia as an unproven form of oral posture training; professional bodies including the American Association of Orthodontists state there is no evidence it improves the jaw. The same article does not mention claims about voice or resonance. Voice science does recognise that tongue position shapes vocal tract resonance during speech, but no study was found testing sustained resting tongue posture as a way to change a person's voice.

name: Throat singing practice

angle.text: Users borrow Tuvan kargyraa and similar overtone singing to train a lower, more resonant voice. The techniques are well documented traditions, but their effect on ordinary speech has not been tested.

summary: Traditional overtone vocal techniques repurposed for lower voice; effect on speech untested.
note: Traditional art form; no studies on changing normal speaking pitch.
currentQuick:
Throat singing is a family of traditional vocal styles from Mongolia, Tuva and Tibet. Some voice-training circles practise low styles hoping for a deeper voice.
No studies have tested whether this changes ordinary speech.
How it works: Singers shape the mouth and throat so particular harmonics are amplified, and some styles use the false vocal folds as a second sound source.
Risks and caveats: Sources reviewed report no health data on the practice; voice clinicians generally discuss strain as a concern with any forced vocal technique.
deepLead:
Throat singing practice, in looksmaxxing and voice-training discussion, refers to using overtone or throat-singing techniques, such as Tuvan kargyraa or Tibetan chant, to train a lower or more resonant voice. Overtone singing is a traditional vocal technique in which a singer shapes the vocal tract so that selected harmonics stand out, producing two audible pitches at once.
The techniques come from Mongolia, Tuva and Tibet, and Western musicians took them up from the 1960s. Some styles add a second sound source from the false vocal folds. No study was found testing whether practising throat singing changes everyday speaking pitch; the Wikipedia article notes acoustic and MRI studies of the technique but reports nothing about voice health effects.

name: Vocal cord filler injection

angle.text: Injection laryngoplasty adds bulk to a vocal fold so the folds meet better, and appearance-focused communities discuss it for a fuller voice. Evidence comes from medical use in vocal fold paralysis and weakness, not cosmetic voice change.

summary: A clinical procedure that bulks a weak vocal fold; evidence is for medical voice disorders, not cosmetic use.
note: Medical procedure by a laryngologist; no cosmetic-use studies.
currentQuick:
Vocal fold injection puts filler into a weak or paralysed vocal fold so the folds close better, improving voice strength. Appearance communities mention it as a way to restore volume.
Studies are in patients with paralysis or tremor, not healthy people seeking cosmetic change.
How it works: Material such as fat, collagen or hyaluronate adds bulk and moves the fold toward the midline so it can vibrate against the other fold.
Risks and caveats: Temporary materials wear off in months, and techniques are not standardised. Specific complications are not detailed in the sources reviewed.
deepLead:
Vocal cord filler injection, medically called injection laryngoplasty or injection augmentation, places material into a vocal fold to add bulk and move it toward the midline so the folds meet better. It is used clinically for vocal fold paralysis and weakness, and appearance-focused communities discuss it as a way to restore a fuller voice.
Materials listed include autologous fat, collagen, hyaluronates, hydroxyapatite and others; effects of temporary materials last roughly 2 to 12 months. Registered trials have examined silk-protein filler, platelet-rich fibrin with fat, and injection for voice tremor, all in patients with medical voice conditions.

name: Laryngoplasty / Adam's apple surgery

angle.text: Chondrolaryngoplasty (tracheal shave) shaves the thyroid cartilage so the Adam's apple is visibly flatter, and is sought for a more feminine neck contour. The result is directly visible, and published series report mostly satisfied patients.

summary: Surgery that shaves down the Adam's apple; usually satisfied patients, rare vocal fold risk.
note: Surgical risks include rare vocal fold injury; no formal studies were reviewed.
currentQuick:
This surgery trims the thyroid cartilage to flatten a prominent Adam's apple. It is common in gender-affirming care and also used cosmetically.
Wikipedia reports most patients are satisfied; complaints concern residual prominence or scarring.
How it works: A surgeon makes a small incision and shaves the cartilage, sometimes endoscopically through the chin or mouth.
Risks and caveats: The vocal folds are close, so rare damage and slight pitch changes are reported. Swelling, bruising and temporary swallowing difficulty are common during about two weeks of recovery.
deepLead:
Chondrolaryngoplasty, popularly called a tracheal shave, reduces the thyroid cartilage that forms the Adam's apple. The nickname is a misnomer because the trachea is not involved.
It is among the more common surgeries for transgender women and is also sought by others uncomfortable with a prominent Adam's apple. It was first described by Francis G. Wolfort and Richard G. Parry in 1975. The voice is usually unaffected, though slight pitch changes have been reported.
